transcript.answer:
ADR-002 (accepted 2026-09-25) settled this when it rejected the PR #261 review comment 4098626654, which proposed dropping the card and letting the model phrase the answer. The card is rendered deterministically, and the assistant's own text is suppressed, for these reasons:
1. Card-rate KPI (SC-006, target ≥ 90% by 2026-Q4). It counts delivery-status questions answered with a rendered card. A prose answer has no measurable denominator, so the KPI is only measurable if the answer is always a card.
2. Thumbs-up KPI (SC-007, target ≥ 80% by 2026-Q4). Ratings attach to card turns, and a prose answer produces no rating.
3. EU AI Act and danish-review compliance. The data-flow record and the docs/danish-review.md rows promise that the customer reads delivery status verbatim from the TMS. A paraphrased delivery time or ETA is a hallucination the pilot cannot afford, because it would damage customer trust.
4. FR-043 of the support-agent-tms-tools spec is being amended to permit a deterministic-render tool. That amendment is the only permitted exception.
5. The not-found card is deterministic for the same reason: the model cannot invent a shipment it did not fetch.
The reviewer's concern was that a rigid card reduces the model's flexibility. The ADR rejected that concern for the reasons above.
sources: issue-318 (Add tools for handling "Hvornår bliver min booking XXXXX leveret?")

judgements.reason: The answer covers the essential points of the gold answer: the card-rate KPI (SC-006, ≥90% by 2026-Q4) needs card turns as its denominator, TMS status must be shown verbatim so a paraphrased ETA is an unaffordable hallucination, and free text was proposed on a PR; its extra details do not contradict the gold.
